# Contributing

Thank you for considering contributing to the Terraform Provider for RustFS! This document provides
guidelines for contributors. Repository conventions that are specific to this codebase (schema
rules, resource patterns, how to add a resource) are in [`AGENTS.md`](../AGENTS.md); the roles and
decision process are in [`GOVERNANCE.md`](../GOVERNANCE.md).

## Getting Started

### Prerequisites

* [Go](https://golang.org/doc/install) 1.27.1 or later (the version in `go.mod`)
* [Docker](https://docs.docker.com/get-docker/) with the `compose` plugin, **or**
  [Podman](https://podman.io) with `podman-compose` — only needed for the acceptance suite
* [Terraform](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/install) 1.0 or later — only needed for the
  acceptance suite
* [Git](https://git-scm.com)

### First Time Setup

```bash
git clone https://github.com/caberdo/terraform-provider-rustfs.git
cd terraform-provider-rustfs
go mod download
make test          # unit tests; the TestAcc* suite skips itself without TF_ACC
```

## Development

### Building

```bash
make build         # ./bin/terraform-provider-rustfs
make install       # install into ~/.terraform.d/plugins for local dev_overrides
```

Add to `~/.terraformrc`:

```hcl
provider_installation {
  dev_overrides {
    "caberdo/rustfs" = "/path/to/terraform-provider-rustfs/bin"
  }
}
```

### Project Structure

```
main.go                        # provider entry point, //go:generate tfplugindocs
provider/                      # the provider package: schema, resources, data sources, tests
  provider.go                  # provider definition, Configure, Resources()/DataSources()
  rustfs_*_resource.go         # resource CRUD implementations (legacy spelling: _ressource.go)
  rustfs_*_datasource.go       # data source implementations (legacy: _data_source.go)
  *_test.go                    # schema/metadata unit tests + TestAcc* acceptance tests
pkg/rustfs/                    # RustFS admin API client (SigV4-signed HTTP)
examples/                      # example Terraform configurations — the source of the documentation
docs/                          # generated by `make generate` — never hand-edit
templates/                     # tfplugindocs templates used by `make generate`
acc_test/docker-compose.yml    # RustFS + test runner used by CI and `make testacc-docker`
scripts/                       # validate-examples, coverage summary, coverage merge
.github/                       # workflows, golangci/goreleaser/dependabot configs, policies
```

See [`ARCHITECTURE.md`](../ARCHITECTURE.md) for what the pieces do at runtime.

## Making Changes

### Coding standards

* `make fmt` (`gofmt`) and `make vet` (`go vet ./...`) before every commit.
* `make lint` runs golangci-lint with the repository configuration
  ([`.github/golangci.yml`](../.github/golangci.yml)); CI runs the same config with a pinned
  linter version, so a green local run means a green CI run.
* Follow idiomatic Go and the conventions in [`AGENTS.md`](../AGENTS.md): append diagnostics then
  bail out on error, human-readable error titles with a contextual detail, `tflog` at CRUD
  boundaries, every schema attribute carries a `Description`.
* All resources implement `ResourceWithImportState`; sensitive fields are `Sensitive: true`; an
  attribute that cannot change in place carries `RequiresReplace()`; computed attributes are set on
  every path or carry `UseStateForUnknown()`.

### Adding New Resources

1. API client methods in `pkg/rustfs/<name>.go` (admin API) and/or through the S3 client.
2. `provider/rustfs_<name>_resource.go` implementing `resource.Resource` and
   `resource.ResourceWithImportState`.
3. Register it in `provider/provider.go` `Resources()`.
4. Describe every schema attribute, mark sensitive fields, validate enums with
   `stringvalidator.OneOf`.
5. Unit tests for the schema and metadata (no server needed) and acceptance tests
   `TestAcc<Name>…`.
6. Add `examples/resources/rustfs_<name>/resource.tf` and run `make generate` so
   `docs/resources/<name>.md` is regenerated — `docs/` is generated output and is diffed in CI.
7. `make validate-examples` to check the example against the schema.

### Changing an existing resource

Terraform type and attribute names are public API: renaming or removing one breaks user state, so it
does not happen outside a major version. A new attribute is optional (or computed) and documented;
an incompatible change needs `RequiresReplace()` and a `BREAKING CHANGES` entry in
[`CHANGELOG.md`](../CHANGELOG.md).

Cite the server behaviour you are encoding (route, status code, payload) in the pull request
description; the RustFS admin API answers `501 NotImplemented` for routes it registered but has not
implemented, so "the route exists" is not proof that a capability works.

## Testing

### Testing policy

* **Major new functionality MUST come with tests in an automated suite.** Resource and data source
  behaviour is asserted with acceptance tests against a real RustFS; parsing, mapping and helper
  logic is asserted with unit tests against `httptest` mocks.
* **Bug fixes MUST come with a regression test** that fails before the fix and passes after it,
  unless the behaviour cannot be reproduced without hardware or a service we cannot script — in that
  case say so in the pull request and describe how you verified the fix by hand.
* Tests are part of the change, not a follow-up: a pull request whose checklist says "tests
  pending" is not ready for review.

### Unit tests

```bash
make test                                     # everything except TestAcc*
go test ./pkg/rustfs/... -v                   # admin API client, mocked with httptest
go test ./provider/... -v -skip '^TestAcc'    # provider schema and metadata
```

### Acceptance tests

They need a RustFS server. Use the shipped environment:

```bash
make testacc-docker      # Docker: rustfs + golang test runner (this is what CI runs)

# Podman: starts RustFS and its replication peer, runs the suite, leaves them
# running. The credentials are deployment inputs, so export them first with the
# values the compose fixture gives its services.
RUSTFS_USER=rustfsadmin RUSTFS_SECRET=rustfsadmin \
  RUSTFS_PEER_ACCESS_KEY=rustfsadmin RUSTFS_PEER_SECRET_KEY=rustfsadmin \
  make testacc-live
```

Run a single test:

```bash
docker compose -f acc_test/docker-compose.yml --profile test run --rm -e TEST_FILTER=TestAccBucketResource test
```

Or point the suite at your own server:

```bash
RUSTFS_ENDPOINT=127.0.0.1:9001 RUSTFS_USER=rustfsadmin RUSTFS_SECRET=rustfsadmin \
  RUSTFS_NOTIFY_TEST_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:9001/health/ready \
  RUSTFS_PEER_ENDPOINT=rustfs-peer:9000 RUSTFS_PEER_ADMIN_ENDPOINT=127.0.0.1:9003 \
  RUSTFS_PEER_S3_ENDPOINT=127.0.0.1:9002 \
  RUSTFS_PEER_ACCESS_KEY=rustfsadmin RUSTFS_PEER_SECRET_KEY=rustfsadmin \
  TF_ACC=1 go test -v ./provider -run TestAcc
```

The compose fixture provisions three server-side prerequisites, so the whole suite runs instead of
skipping:

* `rustfs-peer` is a second RustFS instance. `rustfs_remote_target` validates that its endpoint is
  reachable and that the destination bucket exists and is versioned, so the remote-target and
  bucket-replication tests need it. `RUSTFS_PEER_ENDPOINT` is the peer's S3 data API as seen by the
  primary server (`rustfs-peer:9000`, the API a replication target writes to), while
  `RUSTFS_PEER_ADMIN_ENDPOINT` and `RUSTFS_PEER_S3_ENDPOINT` are the admin and S3 endpoints as seen
  by the test host (`127.0.0.1:9003` and `127.0.0.1:9002`, the peer's published ports). The test
  host's admin endpoint is used to create the peer service account that supplies the second
  credential pair for the remote-target update step. All five values are required; the test skips
  when they are unset and never guesses a port from another endpoint.
* `RUSTFS_NOTIFY_TEST_ENDPOINT` is a webhook endpoint reachable from the RustFS server. The bucket
  notification test registers a `notify_webhook` target named `PRIMARY` and references it as
  `arn:rustfs:sqs::PRIMARY:webhook`; RustFS rejects notification rules when no target is configured.
  The primary server must allow that origin through `RUSTFS_OUTBOUND_ALLOW_ORIGINS`.
* The bucket replication test registers its own `rustfs_remote_target` in Terraform and uses the
  returned ARN as the replication role; RustFS answers `replication config has a stale target` for
  any other role.
* `RUSTFS_SITE_REPLICATION_PEER_ENDPOINT` is the peer as **RustFS** sees it
  (`http://rustfs-peer:9000`) and is the site endpoint `TestAccSiteReplicationResource` hands the
  server. Unlike `RUSTFS_PEER_ENDPOINT` it carries the scheme, and it must not be a loopback
  address: `site-replication/add` refuses one and records the local site from the `Host` header of
  the admin request, so a host-side run against a published port skips this test with the server's
  own explanation.

The LDAP acceptance tests are the exception. No RustFS release can be given an LDAP identity
provider — `help-config-kv` lists `identity_openid` but no `identity_ldap`, the server binary
carries no `RUSTFS_*LDAP*` environment variable, and `add-user` rejects the distinguished names the
LDAP routes expect — so `idp/ldap/add-service-account` answers `target user not exist` on every
supported version and `TestAccLdapServiceAccount` / `TestAccLdapPolicyAttachment_*` always skip.
Their create, read, update, delete and import flows (including every documented import ID form) are
covered by unit tests against a mocked admin API instead: `TestLDAPServiceAccountResource*` and
`TestLDAPPolicyAttachmentResource*`, driving the real resource methods through
`provider/resource_harness_test.go`.

The acceptance container also writes `coverage-acceptance.out`; `make coverage` followed by
`make coverage-merge` merges it with the unit profile (see the coverage table in
[`README.md`](../README.md#testing-and-coverage)).

### Coverage

Merged (unit + acceptance) statement coverage is enforced. `scripts/coverage-gate.sh` compares a
profile against [`.github/coverage-baseline.txt`](./coverage-baseline.txt), and the `Coverage` check
fails a pull request that drops below the floor. The badge and the bar chart in `README.md` are
generated from that same file, so the published number and the enforced floor cannot drift apart.

```bash
make coverage            # unit profile + per-package table
make testacc-docker      # writes coverage-acceptance.out
make coverage-merge      # merge both into coverage-union.out
make coverage-gate       # fail when below the floor
```

To raise the floor: update the `measured_*` and `floor_*` values in `.github/coverage-baseline.txt`
and run `make coverage-readme`. Do that in the same pull request that adds the tests.

## Submitting Changes

### Before submitting

1. `make fmt vet lint` and `make test` pass.
2. Acceptance tests pass for a new or changed resource (`make testacc-docker`).
3. `make generate` produces no `docs/` diff.
4. `make coverage-merge && make coverage-gate` passes, and the coverage floor in
   `.github/coverage-baseline.txt` is raised if the change improved it.
5. The change is described in `CHANGELOG.md` under `Unreleased`.

### Pull request process

1. One feature or fix per pull request.
2. Use a descriptive title referencing the issue (e.g. `feat: add rustfs_group resource (#50)`).
3. Link related issues with `Fixes #123`.
4. Fill in the pull request template — it mirrors the review checklist below.

### Code review

Every change to `main` goes through a pull request; the `protect-main` ruleset requires the
`Lint & Security` and `Test` checks to pass, forbids force-pushes and branch deletion, dismisses
stale reviews on new pushes and requires review threads to be resolved. Reviewers check:

| Area | What has to be true |
|---|---|
| Correctness | The change does what the issue asks, including the error paths; no silently swallowed diagnostics |
| Tests | The testing policy above is met, and the tests fail when the fix is reverted |
| Schema and state | No renamed or removed type/attribute; new attributes are optional or computed, sensitive fields marked, `RequiresReplace()` where an in-place update is impossible; import still works |
| Docs and examples | Schema descriptions present, example added under `examples/`, `docs/` regenerated |
| Security | No credential in code, logs or fixtures; credentials and tokens `Sensitive`; input validation (enums, bounds) for anything user-supplied; no new network egress beyond the configured endpoint |
| Compatibility | RustFS version behaviour cited; capability gaps reported as `UnsupportedFeatureError` rather than raw payloads |

A reviewer requests changes or approves in the pull request. Today the repository has a single
maintainer, so a pull request authored by the maintainer is merged by its author after CI is green —
the ruleset deliberately does not require an approval nobody can give (the decision and its
alternatives are recorded in
[#54](https://github.com/caberdo/terraform-provider-rustfs/issues/54)). Adding a second reviewer
means enabling `required_approving_review_count: 1` and `CODEOWNERS` in the same pull request that
adds them to [`GOVERNANCE.md`](../GOVERNANCE.md).

## Good first issues

Issues labelled [`good first issue`](https://github.com/caberdo/terraform-provider-rustfs/labels/good%20first%20issue)
are scoped so that a first-time contributor can finish them without deep provider knowledge: they
name the file to change, the expected behaviour and the test to extend. If the list is empty, ask in
a new issue or pick a documentation or example improvement — both are genuinely useful here.

## Getting Help

* **GitHub Issues**: bug reports and feature requests
* **Pull Requests**: code contributions, including work in progress
* **Discussions**: ask on an existing issue if you are unsure where your question belongs
